title: Estimating with Whole Numbers, Decimals and Fractions
seo_title: Grade 5 Estimating Worksheets: Decimals, Products and Quotients (TEKS 5.3A, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.3A estimate to determine solutions to mathematical and real-world problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 estimation worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.3A: estimate decimal sums and differences, products, quotients with compatible numbers, fraction sums with benchmarks and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Round or use compatible numbers, then compute.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An estimate is a close answer found with easy numbers. Round, then compute.
  • For decimals, round to the nearest whole number or tenth. For products, round each factor. For quotients, use compatible numbers that divide easily.
  • For fractions, compare each to 0, 1/2 or 1.
  • Use estimates to check whether an exact answer is reasonable.

Examples

Example

Estimate 487 × 32.

487 ≈ 500

32 ≈ 30

500 × 30

Answer: 15,000

Example

Estimate 2,743 ÷ 38.

38 ≈ 40

2,743 ≈ 2,800

2,800 ÷ 40

Answer: 70

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Finding the exact answerAn estimate uses rounded or compatible numbers.
Choosing numbers that do not divide easilyPick a nearby multiple of the rounded divisor.
Rounding to the wrong placeUse the place the question asks for.

faq.a: Estimate to determine solutions to mathematical and real-world problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication or division.
Nearby numbers that work well together, like 2,800 ÷ 40 instead of 2,743 ÷ 38.

faq.q: How do you estimate with fractions?
faq.a: Compare each fraction to 0, 1/2 or 1. 7/8 is about 1, and 3/8 is about 1/2.
When the question asks 'about how many' or when you only need to check if an answer makes sense.
